pbqMapping.testedConcept: Operating-system platform and Windows edition selection
pbqMapping.evidence: Tasks distinguish OS purposes and Windows edition capabilities; no installation or upgrade step is scored.
pbqMapping.correction: Objective metadata narrowed from 1.1-1.3 to 1.1 and 1.3.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Event Viewer, Disk Management, Task Scheduler, and System Configuration
pbqMapping.evidence: Each requirement maps to the appropriate Windows administrative feature or tool.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: sfc, chkdsk, ipconfig, and gpupdate
pbqMapping.evidence: Each task maps a Windows command-line utility to its correct purpose.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Windows network profiles, addressing, sharing, and Remote Desktop settings
pbqMapping.evidence: Every scored field is a Windows setting or client-network configuration value.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: macOS DMG and Time Machine; Linux chmod and apt
pbqMapping.evidence: The tasks correctly distinguish common macOS and Linux features and tools.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Local, SaaS, virtualized, and cloud-synchronized application requirements
pbqMapping.evidence: Deployment clues distinguish application installation requirements and cloud productivity delivery.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Controlled Windows migration, network setup, and application installation
pbqMapping.evidence: The ordered workflow inventories, backs up, migrates, configures connectivity/applications, and validates.
pbqMapping.correction: Objective metadata changed from 1.2-1.7 to 1.2, 1.7, and 1.10.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Physical, technical, and administrative security controls
pbqMapping.evidence: Each scenario maps cleanly to the correct control category.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Windows accounts, BitLocker, share permissions, and auditing
pbqMapping.evidence: All scored fields configure basic Windows security settings.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: WPA settings, client isolation, internal access, and router administration
pbqMapping.evidence: The configurations combine wireless protocol selection with SOHO network hardening.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Vishing, phishing, ransomware, and keylogger recognition
pbqMapping.evidence: The scenarios distinguish malware from social-engineering threats.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: SOHO malware-removal procedure
pbqMapping.evidence: The six steps preserve the approved investigation, quarantine, remediation, validation, and restore-point sequence.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Workstation, mobile-device, and browser hardening
pbqMapping.evidence: Each scenario selects a security control for the specified endpoint type.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Cryptographic erase, overwrite, shredding, and physical destruction
pbqMapping.evidence: Media type, reuse intent, and failure state lead to the correct destruction or sanitization method.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Windows boot, profile, storage, and update issue diagnosis
pbqMapping.evidence: Every symptom is a common Windows operating-system issue with the correct failure classification.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Windows recovery workflow
pbqMapping.evidence: The ordered steps progress from evidence collection through targeted repair, broader recovery, and validation.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Mobile application permission, cache, update, and reinstall troubleshooting
pbqMapping.evidence: Each application symptom maps to the least disruptive appropriate correction.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Lost managed mobile-device response
pbqMapping.evidence: The sequence protects accounts, uses management controls, escalates to wipe, and documents recovery.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Browser hijacking, ransomware, account compromise, and potentially unwanted program recognition
pbqMapping.evidence: Each evidence set identifies the correct PC security issue.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Windows driver, lost mobile device, and ransomware incident response
pbqMapping.evidence: The three rows test Windows OS, mobile security, and PC security troubleshooting; mobile application troubleshooting is not scored.
pbqMapping.correction: Objective metadata narrowed from 3.1-3.4 to 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Incident, asset, knowledge, and change records
pbqMapping.evidence: Each support event is routed to the correct documentation or change-management record.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Backup restoration workflow
pbqMapping.evidence: The sequence protects the source, verifies media, restores full and incremental backups, validates, and documents.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: ESD, battery isolation, ventilation, and electronics recycling
pbqMapping.evidence: Visual callouts identify safety procedures and environmental controls.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Privacy-safe, professional remote-support session
pbqMapping.evidence: The tasks cover authorization, confidentiality, communication, remote-session cleanup, and policy handling.

pbqMapping.testedConcept: Governed scripting and AI-assisted change workflow
pbqMapping.evidence: The ordered process combines safe script design, AI verification, approval, limited deployment, and monitoring.
